name: Bess Lai
life: “I used to defend terrible headlines just because my name was under them.” On Friday, near the approach to Seabright Court, Bess likes to watch the beach traffic thin enough for workers going the other way.
voice: I wrote the first objection when I was seventeen. I returned to disagree with myself at fifty.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a mustard canvas overshirt and a fabric zip pull cut from a school scarf. Bess has a broad nose and a deep dimple on one cheek, with a long plait tucked inside the collar. Bess presses the lips together to keep a smile in during a conversation.
personality: Bess has a talent for getting adversaries to laugh at exactly the same thing. Bess knows better than to expect the laugh to settle what they are arguing about.
agenda: To answer a teenage argument from the viewpoint of later life.
family: Eli Brady is Bess’s younger relative by marriage. Bess asks before bringing somebody along. Eli can always ask for five minutes alone. It keeps a conversation between two people from unexpectedly turning into a family committee. Asked about *The dead man's tab*, Eli says, “I forged my father's signature once. Seeing the real one in the book made me own up.”
connections: Miles Price. One writer's teenage opinion survived a divorce in somebody else's carton. Also in the story is Julian Oh (fellow margin writer).

reactions.situation: A reader asks to erase a personal inscription
reactions.response: Bess puts a clean sheet over the inscription while its writer decides.

reactions.situation: A stranger offers money to cut ahead of an exhausted neighbor
reactions.response: Bess keeps the neighbor's place and finds out whether the stranger needs a different kind of help.

reactions.situation: When people declare an argument over too soon
reactions.response: Bess asks them to describe one concrete thing that will be different tomorrow.
